title: Right derived functor from a class of adapted complexes
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian]. Write $K(\mathcal A)$ for the homotopy category of integer-indexed cochain complexes and $Q_{\mathcal A}:K(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ for localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Equip $K(\mathcal A)$ with its triangulated structure given by shifts and cone triangles [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated]. Let $G:K(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ be an exact functor of triangulated categories [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Let $\mathcal I$ be a class of complexes such that every complex $K$ admits a quasi-isomorphism $K\to I$ with $I\in\mathcal I$, and $G(s)$ is an isomorphism whenever $s:I\to J$ is a quasi-isomorphism between members of $\mathcal I$. Then there are a total right derived functor $RG:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ and a natural transformation $\alpha:G\to RG\circ Q_{\mathcal A}$. They satisfy the following universal property: for every functor $T:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ and natural transformation $\beta:G\to T\circ Q_{\mathcal A}$ there is a unique natural transformation $u:RG\to T$ with $\beta=(u\circ Q_{\mathcal A})\alpha$. For every $I\in\mathcal I$, $\alpha_I:G(I)\to RG(Q_{\mathcal A}I)$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Put C=K(A), W=quasi-isomorphisms and P(K)=(K in I). Let i:P.FullSubcategory→C be the full inclusion and W_P=i⁻¹W. The left calculus of fractions for W induces one for W_P: form each Ore square in C and postcompose its target by a replacement into P; likewise postcompose the target of an equalizing arrow by a replacement. These are the private helper adaptedCalculus and the explicit localizer adaptedLocalizer.

The induced functor F:W_P.Localization→W.Localization is faithful. It suffices to test actual arrows by Mathlib Functor.faithful_of_comp_of_hasLeftCalculusOfFractions. Equality of their images gives a common W-postcomposition equalizing them by MorphismProperty.map_eq_iff_postcomp (a consequence of left-fraction equality). Replace its target into P, giving the same equality already in W_P.Localization. Cancel the image of this W_P-arrow.

F is full. For a morphism between images of P-objects, use Localization.exists_leftFraction to write it as Q(a) Q(b)⁻¹, then replace the common target into P. The resulting numerator and denominator lie in the full subcategory, and the denominator is in W_P. Their fraction maps to the original morphism by naturality of the localization comparison and cancellation. The replacement hypothesis also makes i followed by Q essentially surjective, hence F is essentially surjective. Thus F is an equivalence (adaptedLocalizedEquivalence).

The right-resolution category of every object X is nonempty by replacements. Given two resolutions X→I and X→J, an Ore square and an adapted replacement of its target give a third resolution receiving arrows from both; hence this category is connected (adaptedConnected). To resolve any arrow X→Y, first replace X→I, apply the Ore axiom to this replacement and X→Y, and replace the common target into J. This gives an arrow I→J and a commutative square whose two vertical maps are in W (adaptedArrowResolutions).

Apply Mathlib LocalizerMorphism.IsRightDerivabilityStructure.mk′ from DerivabilityStructure/Constructor.lean to the localized equivalence, connected resolution categories and arrow resolutions. This proves that the full inclusion with W_P and W is a right derivability structure. All inputs have just been constructed, without any closure or invariance assumption on P (adaptedDerivability).

The hypothesis h_inverts says exactly that this right derivability structure derives G. Mathlib LocalizerMorphism.Derives.hasPointwiseRightDerivedFunctor from DerivabilityStructure/Derives.lean supplies pointwise right-derived existence. Take Mathlib G.totalRightDerived Qh W and G.totalRightDerivedUnit Qh W. Their IsRightDerivedFunctor instance is precisely the required universal natural-transformation property at localization.

For I∈I, regard I as an object of P.FullSubcategory and apply Mathlib LocalizerMorphism.Derives.isIso_of_isRightDerivedFunctor to the canonical unit. This gives IsIso (α.app I) and completes the unchanged existential theorem.
